source: captured from three real consultations while this plugin was being developed
why: The sentence-count rule that used to live in parseAdvice rejected all three of these outright as protocol violations. They are kept verbatim so a future change to the parser is judged on the text that actually broke it, not on a hand-written imitation. The values inside are illustrative strings written by a model about a hypothetical log masking function; no credential, host, or user data appears in them.

responses.text: Two things to check before you commit: (1) your quoted-value regex uses `\3` as a backreference to the quote group, but if `name`/`sep` are capture groups 1–2, the quote is group 3 — verify the backreference indexes survive whatever wrapping (named groups, alternation) you add to `(name)`, since a shifted index silently matches wrong quotes or fails closed. (2) Your generalized scheme regex `\b[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:` will match prose like `note:see foo@bar` and `time:12:30@x` — anchor userinfo masking to `://` specifically (scheme `://` userinfo `@`) rather than bare `:`, and confirm the trailing-punctuation behavior on `postgresql://app:pass@host:5432/db` keeps the port/host intact while masking only `app:pass`. On your concerns: suffix heuristics are fine *plus* explicit standalone names (defense in depth, not either/or); regex-order dependence is acceptable if the quoted step is idempotent and the bare step rejects leading quotes as you plan; and yes, mask non-HTTP URL query strings too — a `postgresql://…?password=` leak is as real as an https one, and skipping it is a silent gap.

Your ordering is right (quoted-value before bare, named backreference for the quote), but I'd check three things the working model may have missed: (1) the bare-step lookahead `(?!(?:["']))` only guards the left quote — a value like `secret=abc "def ghi"` or `secret=abc"def"` can still leave a trailing quoted remainder unmasked because the bare rule stops at whitespace, so verify the bare step's value character class is documented as non-space and confirm no orphan quote leaks; (2) the userinfo regex `[^\s<>"'\/@:]+` excludes `@` and `:` from the username but the password class still allows `@`, so `postgresql://app:pa@ss@host` (password containing `@`) will mis-split at the first `@` — decide whether to anchor on the *last* `@` before the host or accept the split; (3) restricting the quoted step to `=`/`:` separators is worth doing, but note it won't exclude whitespace around the separator (`secret = "abc def"`), so either allow `\s*` around sep or accept that form leaks. Separately, verify the `cookie` standalone name under `\b(...)\b` doesn't mask benign `cookie=1` preference values or `Set-Cookie:` fragments in a way that breaks debugging, and confirm the 32+ hex long-token rule isn't keyed on a leading `\b` that env-var values with underscores/dashes near the token boundary can defeat.

I'd check that quoted-value masking runs *before* the bare token rules but that the quote-wrapped match also handles escaped quotes and single-quoted/backtick variants, since `secret='abc def'` and JSON `"key": "sk-… xyz"` are easy to miss otherwise. On your specific questions: the 32+ token rule with hyphen/dot/underscore in its class will still catch `sk-proj-…`/`ds-…` unchanged, but verify the exact class doesn't stop at the first underscore in `ghp_…`-style or `Bearer …` values; `cookie=` masking is low-risk if you require a value following `=` on the same line and exclude bare `cookie=` with empty value, but watch for benign logs like `cookie=disabled` or `cookie_policy=…` (anchor the name with word boundaries and `=`/`:` tail). The real ordering hazard is the reverse of what you asked: if the named-secret step masks `TOKEN=****` first, the long-token regex never sees the value to judge — that's fine — but ensure the whole-quoted rule fires *before* the named-secret rule so the trailing `" def"` isn't left; also confirm multi-match doesn't let a masked placeholder (`****`) be re-consumed or skip an adjacent real secret on the same line.
